bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows Colt’s own revolver books, which document no field strip for a revolver: nothing here comes apart beyond swinging the cylinder out. It is not Heritage’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Heritage exists for this model, and a revolver is the one gun where that costs an owner nothing: Colt’s own operator books document no field strip at all — the maker’s word, not this guide’s caution. Everything a revolver needs is reachable with the cylinder swung out, and that is exactly as far as this guide goes. If yours loads through a gate behind the cylinder instead of swinging out, this is the wrong guide — stop and clean the chambers through the gate.

Listed in Fieldstrip as .38 Special. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Hammer down, cylinder out to the left
steps.action: With the hammer down and your finger off the trigger, work the cylinder release beside the frame — pushed, pulled or pressed, you can see which way yours is shaped to move — and swing the cylinder out to the left.
steps.quote: Open revolver by pulling cylinder latch to the rear and pushing the cylinder out to the left of the revolver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR: 
Colt® Python™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, step 3, p.17
steps.warn: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO CLOSE THE CYLINDER WITH THE HAMMER COCKED. DO NOT SWING OR SLAM THE CYLINDER FORCIBLY INTO PLACE WITH THE HAMMER COCKED. DOING ANY OF THESE ACTIONS COULD DAMAGE THE REVOLVER MECHANISM.

steps.title: Eject, then look and feel every chamber — twice
steps.action: Muzzle up, push the ejector rod firmly to lift everything out of the chambers, and let the rod seat again. Look into every chamber, count them as you go, and run a fingertip across the rear face of the cylinder. Then do it all a second time. A case that will not come out is a stop — never pry it.
steps.quote: Push ejector rod rearward forcing out all live rounds or empty cartridge cases from the chambers. When they are clear of the chambers, remove from revolver.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR: 
Colt® Python™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, step 4, p.17

steps.title: No strip — the maker’s own line
steps.action: Nothing on this revolver comes apart on a bench. The sideplate, the crane and the lockwork behind them belong to Heritage, and the pattern’s own book says so in capitals. The open cylinder is the whole opening, and it is enough.
steps.quote: IMPORTANT: DO NOT FIELD STRIP YOUR REVOLVER. IF YOU DO SO YOU WILL VOID YOUR SERVICE AGREEMENT.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR: 
Colt® Python™ Revolver — Rev. - — Cleaning & Lubrication, closing note, p.18

steps.title: Hard use is a stop, not a strip
steps.action: If the revolver has been in salt air, water, mud or sand, a bench clean is not the cure — that calls for a full strip by someone qualified, which is exactly what the book says.
steps.quote: Note: If the revolver has been used in salt air, water, mud, or sand, it should be completely disassembled, cleaned, and inspected by a competent gunsmith or returned to Colt for service.
steps.cite:
OPERATOR’S MANUAL FOR: 
Colt® Python™ Revolver — Rev. - — Maintenance, p.15

steps.title: Bore from the breech, each chamber on its own
steps.action: With the cylinder out of the way, brush the bore wet with solvent from the breech end through to the muzzle, then dry patches until clean. A bore brush is the wrong size for a chamber: use a chamber brush or a patch on a jag, one chamber at a time, and pay attention to the ring at each chamber mouth.

steps.title: Cylinder face, forcing cone, under the star
steps.action: The grey blast ring on the front face of the cylinder and on the barrel’s rear face comes off with a small brush and a little solvent. Push the ejector rod so the star lifts, brush under it, and let it seat — packed grit under the star is what stops a cylinder closing. A lightly oiled patch through bore and chambers for storage, a trace on the crane, and none into the lockwork.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the forcing cone, the cylinder and the frame for cracks, a bent ejector rod, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Heritage.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Heritage has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Heritage Roscoe, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Heritage exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Heritage, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Bore from the breech end, brush wet then dry patches until clean
Each chamber on its own with a chamber brush
The ring at each chamber mouth
A lightly oiled patch for storage; a dry patch before the next shot

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & FRAME
tasks: Cylinder face and the barrel’s rear face de-ringed
Under the ejector star, then the star seated
A trace of oil on the crane
⛔ No oil into the lockwork from the outside

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Cylinder closed until the latch comes forward
reassembly.action: Hammer down, cylinder pushed gently into the frame until the latch moves forward into its closed position, then the cylinder rotated until the bolt clicks into a notch and locks it. It closes without force or it does not close.
reassembly.quote: With the hammer still in the uncocked position, push the cylinder into the frame until the cylinder latch moves forward into its closed position.

fncheck: Every chamber proven empty twice, cylinder closed and latched. Watch carry-up: draw the hammer back slowly with your thumb, finger OFF the trigger, and watch the cylinder turn and lock as the hand carries it — then, before the hammer ever reaches full cock, ease it back down under your thumb. Do that at two or three chambers. The cylinder should turn to a crisp lock each time, and the latch should sit fully forward on its own. The hammer is never cocked fully and the trigger is never pulled in this check; a revolver that drags, skips or fails to lock goes to Heritage.
